scope: Only the new original-180s/3s process-owner wrapper and its artifact reader; independent from the earlier ELF producer/reader review.
observations: The fixed commands for five product groups enter the existing run_owned implementation with timeout_seconds=180 and cleanup_seconds=3; the request, child stdout/stderr, original receipt and returned API object are retained separately.
The artifact reader independently binds the exact request bytes, command, cwd, paths, environment, original process-owner implementation, 180/3 limits and source/cold identities.

Admission requires zero return code, complete cleanup, ECHILD, reaped leader, no remaining direct children, no cleanup errors, no interrupt/owner error/overflow and only natural lifecycle events; a killed live descendant cannot become a passing product receipt.

The returned API object is compared with the original receipt after removing only supervisor_returncode and receipt_sha256. These are exactly the two fields the original run_owned API appends on a valid normal return.
The adapter rechecks owner evidence after the complete product-artifact read and requires source/receipt identities to remain stable.
The preexisting complete test denominators and explicit whole-native-delivery false fields remain unchanged.
limitations: This review did not parse or execute the new code, any native image, tests, process controller or remote action.
It does not substitute for the 18 focused source/toy controls, future actual five-group execution or full product qualification.
